text: Welcome to your post-operative follow-up. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; to better understand what is happening, can you tell me exactly how many days ago you had your surgery?

text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. speaker: Doctor
text: That shooting pain triggered by chewing and discomfort with earrings suggests the ear canal is still healing or is being irritated; given your history of chronic ear infections and the recent surgery, could you tell me if you have noticed any drainage or a feeling of fullness in your right ear since the operation?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Facial nerve paralysis (Bell's palsy) secondary to post-tympanoplasty infection or trauma.

The shooting pain while eating and discomfort with earrings suggest weakness or paralysis of the facial nerve, which controls the muscles of facial expression and the stapedius (which dampens sound). Can you tell me if you have noticed any difficulty smiling on the right side, drooling, or a change in the taste of food? REQUEST IMAGES: Right ear CT with contrast to evaluate for mastoiditis or facial nerve canal dehiscence.
